title: Black Friday Video Ads From One Photo | AIVideosUGC
description: Create Black Friday video ads from a single product photo and add your discount in your editor. Get a 9:16 or 1:1 clip for Facebook and Instagram today.
h1: Black Friday Video Ads Ready for Your Deal
lead: Black Friday video ads start with a bold product clip made before the sale rush. Upload a photo, describe a striking scene, then add your discount, dates, and countdown in your own editor.
intro: A moving product scene gives your Black Friday offer a visual setting. The sample shows a silver folding e-bike with fat tires standing on a city plaza at golden hour, with glass towers glowing behind it.

The video supplies the moving picture, and you add the deal. You lay prices, percentages, dates, and countdown timers on yourself in CapCut or Ads Manager, so every number is right and easy to change. Make your clips early, then drop in the offer when it's final. It suits bigger-ticket items like bikes, electronics, and appliances.
tip: Leave space for your offer by describing an open area beside the product, like "e-bike on the right, empty plaza and sky on the left."

Download the video, then type the discount, code, and end date in your editor.

ideas.d: Make a second clip with a night-city or neon look to keep the sale going into Monday.

Run the same idea for smaller items like earbuds or smart lights, set on a festive gift table.

faq.q: Which product photo should I upload?
faq.a: Choose a sharp photo of the item you plan to feature and keep the whole product inside the frame.

faq.q: When should I add the discount?
faq.a: Add the final price, code, and sale dates as text after those details are set.

faq.q: Can I use the same video on a store page?
faq.a: Use the same featured product in the video and the destination page so the offer feels connected.

overview.h2: Make the product the fixed point of the sale
overview.d: A Black Friday scene can be vivid without carrying every promotion detail. Choose one product, one visual hook, and one area for your offer; then reuse the visual while the confirmed price, date, or code is finalized.
Use your real stock note, end date, and offer language in the final edit. The generated clip supplies a moving backdrop for the sale rather than inventing inventory, countdowns, or savings.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a sale product with overlay room

items.d: A complete product silhouette gives the sale scene a reliable hero even when the background becomes dramatic.
Choose an angle with sky, wall, floor, or desk space where a discount badge will remain readable.

items.t: Keep the offer out of the photo
items.d: Use a clean image without temporary price stickers so the final promotion can be changed safely.
Say neon street, warm gift table, or focused studio light and keep the product action simple.

results.h2: What the sale clip can do

items.d: A city glow, spotlight, or gift setting makes the product ready for a seasonal ad without embedding changing numbers.
Use 9:16 for Stories and Reels, 1:1 for a feed, 16:9 for a wider placement, or 4:3 and 3:4 when the crop calls for it.
A six-, ten-, fifteen-, or thirty-second version costs 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits; the charge appears before generation.
A gaming headset rests on a dark desk while red and blue light moves across the ear cups and cable.
A folding bike stands on an open city plaza with warm light and clear sky beside the frame for an offer.
A countertop appliance turns slightly under one bright studio beam, ending on its control panel.
Earbuds or a smart light sit on a wrapped gift table with one slow pass for a seasonal bundle.

after_download.h2: Apply the promotion when it is final

items.d: Type the confirmed percentage, price, code, or bundle terms in your editor.
Place the real start and end dates, timezone, and stock wording on a layer you can update.
Add licensed music or a countdown effect only after the visual timing is approved.

fit.h2: Best fits for a sale clip
good: Electronics, bikes, appliances, and gift items
Black Friday and Cyber Monday feeds
Scenes with open space for offer text
not_ideal: A promotion whose terms are not yet confirmed
Claims of scarcity or savings the seller cannot substantiate
